design.quote: Meta-analysis conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of high-dose (≥800 IU/day) and low-dose (<800 IU/day) vitamin D supplementation on preterm infants.

population.quote: vitamin D supplementation on preterm infants

intervention.quote: high-dose (≥800 IU/day) and low-dose (<800 IU/day) vitamin D supplementation

comparator.quote: high-dose (≥800 IU/day) and low-dose (<800 IU/day) vitamin D supplementation

primary_findings.quote: high-dose vitamin D supplementation was associated with increased serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25[OH]D) levels (mean difference 15.62 [13.35-17.88])
800 IU/day significantly increased serum 25(OH)D levels (mean difference 13.99 [9.03-18.95])
reduced the risk of VDD (risk difference -0.21 [-0.32 to -0.10]) compared to 400 IU/day
primary_findings.outcome: Vitamin D deficiency (VDD) (subgroup: 800 IU/day vs 400 IU/day)

limitations_stated.value: The certainty of the evidence ranges from moderate to very low.
limitations_stated.quote: The certainty of the evidence ranges from moderate to very low.
